q: 你到___地铁站，先给我打个电话，我再去接你。
zh: 你到了地铁站，先给我打个电话，我再去接你。
py: nǐ dào le dì tiě zhàn xiān gěi wǒ dǎ ge diàn huà wǒ zài qù jiē nǐ
en: Once you get to the subway station, call me first and then I'll come to meet you.
why: 到了 + place sets up 'once you've arrived' before the next steps (先…再…), so 了 follows 到. 过 means you have been there before, and 着 does not fit an arrival.

q: 这个球场太小___，十个人不能一起踢。
zh: 这个球场太小了，十个人不能一起踢。
py: zhè ge qiú chǎng tài xiǎo le shí ge rén bù néng yī qǐ tī
en: This pitch is too small for ten people to play together.
why: 'Too small' is a complete remark with 太…了. 地 and 着 are not used after an adjective at the end of a clause.

q: 昨天我们打___球就去吃火锅___。
zh: 昨天我们打了球就去吃火锅了。
py: zuó tiān wǒ men dǎ le qiú jiù qù chī huǒ guō le
en: Yesterday we went for hotpot as soon as we'd finished playing ball.
why: A past sequence takes 了 after the first verb (打了球) and a closing 了 after the last step (吃火锅了). 着 would mean playing while going, and 的 and 地 are not verb endings.

zh: 我们已经走了一个小时了。
py: wǒ men yǐ jīng zǒu le yī ge xiǎo shí le
en: We've already been walking for an hour.
why: 已经 goes with the double-了 pattern: 了 right after 走 and again at the end. 已经 stays before the verb phrase.

zh: 我不想去健身房了。
py: wǒ bù xiǎng qù jiàn shēn fáng le
en: I don't want to go to the gym any more.
why: 'Not any more' is 不 + verb phrase + 了, so 了 goes at the very end. 没 would only deny a past event.

q: 你吃___饭再去游泳，不然会不舒服。
zh: 你吃了饭再去游泳，不然会不舒服。
py: nǐ chī le fàn zài qù yóu yǒng bù rán huì bù shū fu
en: Eat first and then go swimming, or you'll feel unwell.
why: 'Do A, then B' with 再 puts 了 after the first verb, before its object. 着 would mean the eating is still in progress, so 再 could not move on to swimming.

zh: 这个包太贵了。
py: zhè ge bāo tài guì le
en: This bag is too expensive!
why: 'Too expensive' replaces 很 with 太 and closes with 了, as a complete remark.

zh: 昨天地铁站里人很多。
py: zuó tiān dì tiě zhàn lǐ rén hěn duō
en: The subway station was crowded yesterday.
why: A past description with 很 + adjective is a state, so it takes no 了; 昨天 carries the past. 昨天 may come before or after 地铁站里.

src_py: wǒ cháng qù nà jiā kā fēi guǎn
task: Say you don't go there any more.
zh: 我不去那家咖啡馆了。
py: wǒ bù qù nà jiā kā fēi guǎn le
en: I'm not going to that café any more.
why: 'Not any more' is 不 + verb + 了, with 了 at the end. 没去 would only say you did not go on one occasion. The object 那家咖啡馆 may also be fronted as a topic.

q: 我累了，不想跑步___。
zh: 我累了，不想跑步了。
py: wǒ lèi le bù xiǎng pǎo bù le
en: I'm tired, I don't want to run any more.
why: 'Not any more' is 不 + verb + 了, with 了 at the end. 吗 would make it a question, and 着 and 过 do not close a negative wish.

q: 我们吃___饭，现在去踢球吧。
zh: 我们吃了饭，现在去踢球吧。
py: wǒ men chī le fàn xiàn zài qù tī qiú ba
en: We've eaten, so let's go and play football now.
why: 'Eat, then go' puts 了 after the first verb, before its object, since the eating is done before the next step. 着 would mean eating is still going on, which clashes with 现在去踢球.

src_py: tā tī le yī ge xiǎo shí qiú
task: Say he has been playing for an hour and is still playing.
zh: 他踢了一个小时球了。
py: tā tī le yī ge xiǎo shí qiú le
en: He has been playing football for an hour now.
why: 'So far, and still going' adds a final 了 to the 了 after the verb. 球 can follow the verb phrase or be fronted before 踢了.

s: 小王去年在了北京。
zh: 小王去年在北京。
py: xiǎo wáng qù nián zài běi jīng
en: Xiao Wang was in Beijing last year.
why: 在 says where someone was, a state, so 在了 is not used for 'was at'. 去年 alone supplies the past.
s_py: xiǎo wáng qù nián zài le běi jīng

zh: 这个地方太吵了。
py: zhè ge dì fang tài chǎo le
en: This place is too noisy.
why: A 太 remark closes with 了, so 了 comes last, after the adjective. 太 sits directly before the adjective.

zh: 这家球鞋店的东西太贵了。
py: zhè jiā qiú xié diàn de dōng xi tài guì le
en: Things in this sports-shoe shop are too expensive.
why: 太贵了 is the complete remark, with 了 last. The modifier 这家球鞋店的 must stay in front of 东西.

s: 我昨天去了一趟超市。
zh: 我昨天去了一趟超市。
py: wǒ zuó tiān qù le yī tàng chāo shì
en: I made a trip to the supermarket yesterday.
why: A finished action with a counted amount (一趟) takes 了 right after the verb, so 去了一趟 is correct. Nothing is missing, so the sentence is fine.

s: 他以前是游泳教练，现在去别的城市工作了。
zh: 他以前是游泳教练，现在去别的城市工作了。
py: tā yǐ qián shì yóu yǒng jiào liàn xiàn zài qù bié de chéng shì gōng zuò le
en: He used to be a swimming coach; now he has gone to work in another city.
why: 是 stays bare for the past state (以前是), while 现在…了 reports a new situation: he has moved on. Each 了 is where it belongs.

q: 听说他的网球越打越好，现在已经能参加比赛___。
zh: 听说他的网球越打越好，现在已经能参加比赛了。
py: tīng shuō tā de wǎng qiú yuè dǎ yuè hǎo xiàn zài yǐ jīng néng cān jiā bǐ sài le
en: I hear his tennis keeps getting better, and he can already enter matches now.
why: 已经能 reports a new ability that did not exist before, so the sentence ends in 了. 过 would mean he has joined matches before, and 着 or 的 would leave the change unmarked.

q: 上大学的时候，我一般每天晚上都在操场跑___半个小时步。
zh: 上大学的时候，我一般每天晚上都在操场跑半个小时步。
py: shàng dà xué de shí hou wǒ yī bān měi tiān wǎn shang dōu zài cāo chǎng pǎo bàn ge xiǎo shí bù
en: When I was at university I usually jogged on the sports ground for half an hour every evening.
why: 一般 and 每天晚上 make this a routine, so even with a duration (半个小时) there is no 了. 了 would describe one half-hour run that is over.

q: 我们没找到___那家书店。
zh: 我们没找到那家书店。
py: wǒ men méi zhǎo dào nà jiā shū diàn
en: We didn't find that bookshop.
why: 没 + 找到 already reports the failure; adding 了 would claim the finding happened. In a denial the verb stays bare.

q: 我们下___班就去爬山。
zh: 我们下了班就去爬山。
py: wǒ men xià le bān jiù qù pá shān
en: We'll go hiking as soon as we get off work.
why: 'As soon as A, then B' puts 了 right after the first verb, even for a plan. 着 and 地 do not fit 下班, and 过 is about a past experience.

s: 我们昨天了踢两个小时球。
zh: 我们昨天踢了两个小时球。
py: wǒ men zuó tiān tī le liǎng ge xiǎo shí qiú
en: We played ball for two hours yesterday.
why: 了 attaches directly after the verb it completes (踢了); it can never stand in front of the verb.
s_py: wǒ men zuó tiān le tī liǎng ge xiǎo shí qiú

task: Say it has turned cold now.
zh: 天气冷了。
py: tiān qì lěng le
en: It's gotten cold.
why: A change of state ends in 了. Dropping 很 removes the plain-description reading: 很冷 alone describes how things are, not that something changed.

s: 我小时候常常去了游泳池。
zh: 我小时候常常去游泳池。
py: wǒ xiǎo shí hou cháng cháng qù yóu yǒng chí
en: As a child I often went to the swimming pool.
why: 常常 marks a repeated habit, and habits take no 了 even in the past. 去了 would describe one finished trip, which clashes with 常常.

q: 他今天早上跑___五公里。
zh: 他今天早上跑了五公里。
py: tā jīn tiān zǎo shang pǎo le wǔ gōng lǐ
en: He ran five kilometres this morning.
why: A completed run with a counted distance needs 了 straight after the verb, before 五公里. 着 and 在 describe an action in progress, and 的 does not belong after a verb here.

src_py: xiān chī fàn zài qù kàn bǐ sài
task: Rewrite with 了: eat first, then go.
zh: 吃了饭再去看比赛。
py: chī le fàn zài qù kàn bǐ sài
en: Eat first and then go and watch the match.
why: 'Do A, then B' puts 了 right after the first verb (吃了饭), and 再 introduces the next step.

s: 我以前在上海住了三年，后来搬到了北京。
zh: 我以前在上海住了三年，后来搬到了北京。
py: wǒ yǐ qián zài shàng hǎi zhù le sān nián hòu lái bān dào le běi jīng
en: I used to live in Shanghai for three years and later moved to Beijing.
why: 以前 and 后来 make the three years a closed period, so one 了 after 住 is right; a second final 了 would say he still lives there.

src_py: zhè jiā diàn yǒu miàn bāo
task: Say there is no bread left.
zh: 这家店没有面包了。
py: zhè jiā diàn méi yǒu miàn bāo le
en: This shop has no bread left.
why: 'None left' is 没有 + noun + 了: 没有 replaces 有 and 了 closes the sentence.

q: 他腿受伤以后就___踢球___，现在只在旁边看。
zh: 他腿受伤以后就不踢球了，现在只在旁边看。
py: tā tuǐ shòu shāng yǐ hòu jiù bù tī qiú le xiàn zài zhǐ zài páng biān kàn
en: After his leg injury he stopped playing football; now he only watches from the side.
why: 'Stopped doing X' is 不 + verb + 了. 别 is a command, and 着 or 吗 cannot mark the change from playing to not playing.

zh: 他昨天下了班就去健身房了。
py: tā zuó tiān xià le bān jiù qù jiàn shēn fáng le
en: Yesterday he went to the gym right after work.
why: A past sequence has 了 on the first verb (下了班) and a closing 了 after the last step. 昨天 can come before or after 他.

q: 这家健身房的人___多___，我不想去。
zh: 这家健身房的人太多了，我不想去。
py: zhè jiā jiàn shēn fáng de rén tài duō le wǒ bù xiǎng qù
en: There are too many people in this gym, so I don't want to go.
why: 'Too many' is 太 + adjective + 了. 很, 非常 and 特别 mean 'very', do not take a closing 了, and cannot combine with these endings.

q: 她打___两个小时网球，累得走不动了。
zh: 她打了两个小时网球，累得走不动了。
py: tā dǎ le liǎng ge xiǎo shí wǎng qiú lèi de zǒu bù dòng le
en: She played tennis for two hours and was too tired to walk.
why: The two hours are finished and led to her being tired, so 了 follows 打. 着 would keep her playing, 过 is only 'have ever played', and 地 does not attach to a verb.

q: 我打___两年乒乓球___，水平还是很差。
zh: 我打了两年乒乓球了，水平还是很差。
py: wǒ dǎ le liǎng nián pīng pāng qiú le shuǐ píng hái shì hěn chà
en: I've been playing table tennis for two years and I'm still poor at it.
why: 'Two years so far, and still going' needs 了 after the verb and again at the end. 着 cannot sit before a duration, and a final 着 does not close the sentence.

src_py: wǒ shàng wǔ qù le qiú chǎng
task: Make it negative: I didn't go.
zh: 我上午没去球场。
py: wǒ shàng wǔ méi qù qiú chǎng
en: I didn't go to the court in the morning.
why: To deny a finished action use 没 before the verb and drop 了. 上午 can come before or after 我.

q: 这条路上的车太多___，骑自行车一点儿也不安全。
zh: 这条路上的车太多了，骑自行车一点儿也不安全。
py: zhè tiáo lù shàng de chē tài duō le qí zì xíng chē yī diǎn r yě bù ān quán
en: There are too many cars on this road; cycling is not safe at all.
why: 车太多 is a full remark, so it ends in 了. 的 would turn 太多 into a modifier and break the clause; 着 and 过 do not follow adjectives.

q: 那天晚上我觉得___这场球赛很精彩。
zh: 那天晚上我觉得这场球赛很精彩。
py: nà tiān wǎn shang wǒ jué de zhè chǎng qiú sài hěn jīng cǎi
en: That night I thought the match was very exciting.
why: 觉得 reports an opinion, a state, so it takes no 了 even in the past. 觉得了 does not mean 'thought'; 那天晚上 supplies the time.

q: 我昨天踢___两个小时足球。
zh: 我昨天踢了两个小时足球。
py: wǒ zuó tiān tī le liǎng ge xiǎo shí zú qiú
en: I played football for two hours yesterday.
why: One finished event with a counted duration takes 了 right after the verb. 过 would only say it is something I have experienced, and 着 and 的 cannot mark completion.

q: 他现在会游蛙泳___，不用再学了。
zh: 他现在会游蛙泳了，不用再学了。
py: tā xiàn zài huì yóu wā yǒng le bù yòng zài xué le
en: He can swim breaststroke now, so he doesn't need to learn any more.
why: 现在会 marks a new ability: he could not before, he can now, so 了 ends the clause. 过 would mean he has swum breaststroke at some time; 着 and 的 mark nothing here.

s: 他以前是了足球运动员。
zh: 他以前是足球运动员。
py: tā yǐ qián shì zú qiú yùn dòng yuán
en: He used to be a football player.
why: 是 is not an action that can be completed, so 是了 never means 'was'. 以前 alone gives the past.

s: 公园里没有人了。
zh: 公园里没有人了。
py: gōng yuán lǐ méi yǒu rén le
en: There's no one left in the park.
why: 没有 + noun + 了 means 'none left'. The 了 is part of that pattern and is correct, unlike 没 + verb for a plain past denial.

q: 我昨天___去踢球。
zh: 我昨天没去踢球。
py: wǒ zuó tiān méi qù tī qiú
en: I didn't go and play football yesterday.
why: To deny a past event use 没 + verb, with no 了. 不 is for habits, will and intention, and 别 and 不要 give orders.

q: 昨天公园里人很多，大家都很高兴___。
zh: 昨天公园里人很多，大家都很高兴。
py: zuó tiān gōng yuán lǐ rén hěn duō dà jiā dōu hěn gāo xìng
en: Yesterday the park was crowded and everyone was happy.
why: 很高兴 describes how people felt, a state, and 昨天 already places it in the past. 了 would suggest they had just become happy, which is not what the sentence says.

s: 太贵的球拍我不买。
zh: 太贵的球拍我不买。
py: tài guì de qiú pāi wǒ bù mǎi
en: I won't buy a racket that's too expensive.
why: Here 太贵 only modifies 球拍 and is not a complete remark, so it takes no 了. 太贵了 is for the standalone 'It's too expensive!'.

zh: 他已经会打乒乓球了。
py: tā yǐ jīng huì dǎ pīng pāng qiú le
en: He can already play table tennis.
why: 已经会 reports a new ability, so 了 closes the sentence. 已经 sits before 会, and 了 cannot move before the object.

q: 今天___冷，我们可以在外面踢球。
zh: 今天不太冷，我们可以在外面踢球。
py: jīn tiān bù tài lěng wǒ men kě yǐ zài wài miàn tī qiú
en: It's not very cold today, so we can play football outside.
why: Only 不太 fits 'so we can play outside': it means 'not very cold' and takes no 了. 太, 很 and 非常 all say it is cold, and 太冷 would also need 了.

q: 我儿子都五岁___，还不会游泳。
zh: 我儿子都五岁了，还不会游泳。
py: wǒ ér zi dōu wǔ suì le hái bù huì yóu yǒng
en: My son is already five and still can't swim.
why: 都…了 says 'already': he has reached a new age, and a changed age ends in 了. Without it 都五岁 is left hanging, and 过 and 的 do not mark change.

q: 我在路口等___十分钟，公交车才来。
zh: 我在路口等了十分钟，公交车才来。
py: wǒ zài lù kǒu děng le shí fēn zhōng gōng jiāo chē cái lái
en: I waited ten minutes at the junction before the bus finally came.
why: 等 completed a counted ten minutes, so 了 goes right after the verb. 着 means 'while waiting' and cannot take a duration; 过 would be about experience.

zh: 小王在地铁站等了二十分钟。
py: xiǎo wáng zài dì tiě zhàn děng le èr shí fēn zhōng
en: Xiao Wang waited twenty minutes at the subway station.
why: 等了 takes the counted duration straight after it. The place phrase 在地铁站 comes before the verb, never after the duration.

zh: 他学了三个月游泳了。
py: tā xué le sān ge yuè yóu yǒng le
en: He has been learning to swim for three months and is still at it.
why: 'Three months so far, still going' needs 了 after the verb and 了 at the very end. The final 了 cannot come before 游泳.

src_py: tā pǎo le wǔ gōng lǐ
task: Add 已经 and say he has run five kilometres so far.

py: tā yǐ jīng pǎo le wǔ gōng lǐ le
en: He has already run five kilometres.

q: 他在公园里骑___一个小时自行车，出了很多汗。
zh: 他在公园里骑了一个小时自行车，出了很多汗。
py: tā zài gōng yuán lǐ qí le yī ge xiǎo shí zì xíng chē chū le hěn duō hàn

q: 昨天下午我在___体育馆，没看到他。
zh: 昨天下午我在体育馆，没看到他。
py: zuó tiān xià wǔ wǒ zài tǐ yù guǎn méi kàn dào tā
en: I was at the gym yesterday afternoon and didn't see him.

q: 小时候我常常和哥哥一起去河边钓___鱼。
zh: 小时候我常常和哥哥一起去河边钓鱼。
py: xiǎo shí hou wǒ cháng cháng hé gē ge yī qǐ qù hé biān diào yú
en: As a child I often went fishing by the river with my older brother.
why: 常常 and 小时候 describe a repeated childhood habit, so the verb takes no 了 even though it is in the past. 了 would suggest one finished trip.

q: 周末我们在公园打___一下午羽毛球。

py: zhōu mò wǒ men zài gōng yuán dǎ le yī xià wǔ yǔ máo qiú

q: 已经八点___，比赛马上要开始了。
zh: 已经八点了，比赛马上要开始了。
py: yǐ jīng bā diǎn le bǐ sài mǎ shàng yào kāi shǐ le
en: It's already eight o'clock and the match is about to start.

q: 你的球打得太好___！

py: nǐ de qiú dǎ de tài hǎo le
en: You play so well!
why: An exclamation with 太 + adjective closes with 了. 吗 would turn it into a question, and 的 would leave the remark hanging.

zh: 他每个周末都去游泳馆。
py: tā měi ge zhōu mò dōu qù yóu yǒng guǎn
en: He goes to the swimming pool every weekend.
why: 每个周末都 marks a habit, so the verb takes no 了, which is why the spare tile is unused. 每个周末 can open the sentence or follow 他.

q: 他们踢___一个小时___，比分还是零比零。

py: tā men tī le yī ge xiǎo shí le bǐ fēn hái shì líng bǐ líng
en: They've been playing for an hour and it's still nil-nil.
why: 还是零比零 shows the game is still going, so the hour is 'so far': 了 after 踢 and 了 at the end. Without both, the hour sounds closed off.

q: 我们的水喝完了，没有水___。
zh: 我们的水喝完了，没有水了。
py: wǒ men de shuǐ hē wán le méi yǒu shuǐ le
en: We've drunk all our water and have none left.
why: 'Run out' is 没有 + noun + 了, ending with 了. 着 and 的 cannot close it, and 吗 would turn it into a question.

s: 我女儿了八岁。
zh: 我女儿八岁了。
py: wǒ nǚ ér bā suì le
en: My daughter is eight now.
why: The change-of-state 了 ends the sentence after the age; it cannot come before the number.
s_py: wǒ nǚ ér le bā suì

s: 明天你下了班给我打个电话。
zh: 明天你下了班给我打个电话。
py: míng tiān nǐ xià le bān gěi wǒ dǎ ge diàn huà
en: Call me tomorrow after you get off work.
why: 'After A, then B' uses 了 after the first verb even for the future, because it marks A as done before B. 明天 does not forbid it.

zh: 我们下了课就去打球。
py: wǒ men xià le kè jiù qù dǎ qiú
en: We'll go and play ball as soon as class is over.
why: 下了课 gives the first step as done, and 就 starts the second. Even for a plan, 了 follows the first verb.

q: 球票卖完了，我们没有票___，只能在家看电视。
zh: 球票卖完了，我们没有票了，只能在家看电视。
py: qiú piào mài wán le wǒ men méi yǒu piào le zhǐ néng zài jiā kàn diàn shì
en: The tickets are sold out; we have none left and can only watch TV at home.
why: 'Have none left' is 没有 + noun + 了, with 了 at the end. 吗 would make it a question, and 着 and 的 cannot close it.

src_py: tā mǎi le nà zhāng qiú piào
zh: 他没买那张球票。
py: tā méi mǎi nà zhāng qiú piào
en: He didn't buy that match ticket.
why: Negate with 没 and delete 了: 没买, not 没买了. A specific object (那张球票) changes nothing.

q: 路上堵车，所以我们没有在九点以前到___体育馆。
zh: 路上堵车，所以我们没有在九点以前到体育馆。
py: lù shang dǔ chē suǒ yǐ wǒ men méi yǒu zài jiǔ diǎn yǐ qián dào tǐ yù guǎn
en: There was a traffic jam, so we didn't get to the gym before nine.
why: 没有 denies the arrival, so 到 takes no 了. 到了 would claim the arrival happened, and 过 would say 'never been there', which is not what the sentence is about.

s: 这家球馆太了大。
zh: 这家球馆太大了。
py: zhè jiā qiú guǎn tài dà le
en: This sports hall is too big.
why: 了 closes the whole 太 + adjective remark; it cannot sit between 太 and the adjective.
s_py: zhè jiā qiú guǎn tài le dà

zh: 我吃了饭就去公园。
py: wǒ chī le fàn jiù qù gōng yuán
en: I'll go to the park once I've eaten.
why: In 'after A, then B', 了 is attached to the first verb (吃了) and 就 introduces the next step. 我 may open the sentence or follow 吃了饭.

q: 他去年是___我们队的教练。
zh: 他去年是我们队的教练。
py: tā qù nián shì wǒ men duì de jiào liàn
en: He was our team's coach last year.
why: 是 is a state, not an action that can be completed, so 是了 is never 'was'. 去年 alone puts it in the past.

q: 这条路太远___，我们坐出租车去吧。
zh: 这条路太远了，我们坐出租车去吧。
py: zhè tiáo lù tài yuǎn le wǒ men zuò chū zū chē qù ba
en: It's too far this way; let's take a taxi.
why: 'Too far' is a complete remark with 太…了, so 了 closes it. 着 and 过 cannot follow an adjective this way.

q: 我明天下___课就去球场找你。
zh: 我明天下了课就去球场找你。
py: wǒ míng tiān xià le kè jiù qù qiú chǎng zhǎo nǐ
en: I'll come and find you at the court as soon as class is over tomorrow.
why: Even though it is tomorrow, 'once class is over, then ...' uses 了 after the first verb. 了 marks completion before the next step, not past time.

s: 我不了去游泳。
zh: 我不去游泳了。
py: wǒ bù qù yóu yǒng le
en: I'm not going swimming any more.
why: 'Not any more' puts 了 at the end of the clause, after 不 + the verb phrase, not between 不 and the verb.
s_py: wǒ bù le qù yóu yǒng

zh: 他上午游了一千米。
py: tā shàng wǔ yóu le yī qiān mǐ
en: He swam a thousand metres in the morning.
why: 游了 keeps 了 right after the verb, before the counted distance. 上午 may come before or after 他 but stays ahead of the verb.

q: 天黑___，我们回家吧。
zh: 天黑了，我们回家吧。
py: tiān hēi le wǒ men huí jiā ba
en: It's dark now, so let's go home.
why: Dark has just arrived, a change from before, so the clause ends in 了. 着 would describe a state with no change, and 过 is for experience.

q: 我已经___喝可乐___，现在只喝水。
zh: 我已经不喝可乐了，现在只喝水。
py: wǒ yǐ jīng bù hē kě lè le xiàn zài zhǐ hē shuǐ
en: I don't drink cola any more; now I only drink water.
why: 已经 plus 不 + verb needs a closing 了 for 'no longer'. 别 is a command, and 着 or 吗 would not mark the change.

s: 我们以前经常在这个球场踢了球。
zh: 我们以前经常在这个球场踢球。
py: wǒ men yǐ qián jīng cháng zài zhè ge qiú chǎng tī qiú
en: We often used to play ball on this pitch.
why: 经常 marks a repeated habit, so 踢 takes no 了; with 了 it would be one finished event, which clashes with 经常.
s_py: wǒ men yǐ qián jīng cháng zài zhè ge qiú chǎng tī le qiú

q: 昨天比赛结束以后，教练请我们每个人吃___一碗面。
zh: 昨天比赛结束以后，教练请我们每个人吃了一碗面。
py: zuó tiān bǐ sài jié shù yǐ hòu jiào liàn qǐng wǒ men měi ge rén chī le yī wǎn miàn
en: After the match yesterday, the coach treated each of us to a bowl of noodles.
why: 吃 happened once, yesterday, with a counted object (一碗面), so 了 follows 吃. 着 describes a state while eating, which does not fit a treat that was finished.

q: 太晚了，我们不去夜市___，回家休息吧。
zh: 太晚了，我们不去夜市了，回家休息吧。
py: tài wǎn le wǒ men bù qù yè shì le huí jiā xiū xi ba
en: It's too late; we're not going to the night market after all. Let's go home and rest.
why: A changed plan ('not going after all') is 不 + verb + 了. 的 and 着 do not close it, and 吗 would make the clause a question.

s: 他昨天没去了体育馆。
zh: 他昨天没去体育馆。
py: tā zuó tiān méi qù tǐ yù guǎn
en: He didn't go to the gym yesterday.
why: 没 already denies the event, so 了 cannot be added after the verb.
s_py: tā zuó tiān méi qù le tǐ yù guǎn

q: 前面就是地铁站，我们快到___。
zh: 前面就是地铁站，我们快到了。
py: qián miàn jiù shì dì tiě zhàn wǒ men kuài dào le
en: The subway station is just ahead; we're almost there.
why: 快…了 means 'about to', a change on its way, so 了 ends the sentence. 过 and 着 cannot close 快到, and 的 leaves the phrase unfinished.

src_py: tā men kàn le nà chǎng bǐ sài
zh: 他们没看那场比赛。
py: tā men méi kàn nà chǎng bǐ sài
en: They didn't watch that match.
why: 没 already says the watching did not happen, so 了 is removed. 没看了 would contradict itself.

q: 小时候他很不喜欢___运动，现在却每天都去健身房。
zh: 小时候他很不喜欢运动，现在却每天都去健身房。
py: xiǎo shí hou tā hěn bù xǐ huan yùn dòng xiàn zài què měi tiān dōu qù jiàn shēn fáng
en: As a child he really disliked exercise, but now he goes to the gym every day.
why: 喜欢 is a feeling, a state, so 了 is left out even for the past; 小时候 shows the time. 了 would read as a change that has just happened, which conflicts with the contrast.

q: 我们昨天走___三公里才到公园。
zh: 我们昨天走了三公里才到公园。
py: wǒ men zuó tiān zǒu le sān gōng lǐ cái dào gōng yuán
en: Yesterday we walked three kilometres before we reached the park.
why: 走 covered a counted distance and finished, so 了 comes right after the verb. 着 cannot be followed by a distance; 的 and 地 are not verb endings.

q: 这双球鞋太贵___，我不买。
zh: 这双球鞋太贵了，我不买。
py: zhè shuāng qiú xié tài guì le wǒ bù mǎi
en: These sports shoes are too expensive, so I won't buy them.
why: A 太 remark ends in 了: 太贵了. 的 turns it into a noun phrase, and 吗 and 吧 change it into a question or suggestion.

q: 从早上到现在，他一共跑___二十公里___，还想继续跑。
zh: 从早上到现在，他一共跑了二十公里了，还想继续跑。
py: cóng zǎo shang dào xiàn zài tā yī gòng pǎo le èr shí gōng lǐ le hái xiǎng jì xù pǎo
en: Since this morning he has run twenty kilometres in all and wants to keep running.
why: 到现在 and 还想继续 show the total is 'so far', not closed: 了 after 跑 and a second 了 at the end. 吗 would turn it into a question.

q: 他今天早上没跑___步。
zh: 他今天早上没跑步。
py: tā jīn tiān zǎo shang méi pǎo bù
en: He didn't go running this morning.
why: 没 denies the event outright, so there is nothing for 了 to mark as completed. 着 and 的 are not endings that can follow 没跑.

q: 本来我想骑车去，可是下大雨了，我只好不骑___，改坐地铁。
zh: 本来我想骑车去，可是下大雨了，我只好不骑了，改坐地铁。
py: běn lái wǒ xiǎng qí chē qù kě shì xià dà yǔ le wǒ zhǐ hǎo bù qí le gǎi zuò dì tiě
en: I originally meant to cycle, but it started pouring, so I had to give up on it and take the subway.
why: 'Changed my mind, not doing it' is 不 + verb + 了, with 了 at the end. 着, 过 and 的 do not mark the change of plan.

q: 他们经常在这家球馆打___羽毛球。
zh: 他们经常在这家球馆打羽毛球。
py: tā men jīng cháng zài zhè jiā qiú guǎn dǎ yǔ máo qiú
en: They often play badminton at this sports hall.
why: 经常 marks a habit, so no 了 after 打. 了 would turn it into a single completed game, and 着 and 的 do not fit.

q: 以前我们总是坐___地铁去体育馆。
zh: 以前我们总是坐地铁去体育馆。
py: yǐ qián wǒ men zǒng shì zuò dì tiě qù tǐ yù guǎn
en: We always used to take the subway to the gym.
why: 总是 marks a repeated routine in the past, which takes no 了. With 了, 坐了地铁去 would describe a single trip that has been completed.

zh: 下雨了，我们不去爬山了。
py: xià yǔ le wǒ men bù qù pá shān le
en: It's raining, so we're not going hiking after all.
why: The rain is a new situation, so the first clause ends in 了; the changed plan 不去爬山 also ends in 了. Each clause closes with its own 了.

q: 上周我没买___球票，所以今天不能去看比赛。
zh: 上周我没买球票，所以今天不能去看比赛。
py: shàng zhōu wǒ méi mǎi qiú piào suǒ yǐ jīn tiān bù néng qù kàn bǐ sài
en: I didn't buy a ticket last week, so I can't go to the match today.
why: 没 already says the purchase did not happen, so 了 cannot follow 买. 了 marks completion and clashes with 没.

s: 他还没吃了午饭。
zh: 他还没吃午饭。
py: tā hái méi chī wǔ fàn
en: He hasn't had lunch yet.
why: 还没 negates the event, so the verb stays bare and 了 cannot follow 吃.
s_py: tā hái méi chī le wǔ fàn

q: 昨天我很忙，我___去游泳，也___去跑步。
zh: 昨天我很忙，我没去游泳，也没去跑步。
py: zuó tiān wǒ hěn máng wǒ méi qù yóu yǒng yě méi qù pǎo bù
en: I was busy yesterday: I didn't go swimming and I didn't go running either.
why: Denying two past events uses 没 + verb each time, with no 了. 不 would sound like a refusal or a plan, and 别 is a command.

s: 比赛快要开始了。
zh: 比赛快要开始了。
py: bǐ sài kuài yào kāi shǐ le
en: The match is about to start.
why: 快要…了 frames something about to happen, and the final 了 is required, so this sentence is correct.

q: 我刚才在地铁站买___一张去机场的票。
zh: 我刚才在地铁站买了一张去机场的票。
py: wǒ gāng cái zài dì tiě zhàn mǎi le yī zhāng qù jī chǎng de piào
en: I just bought a ticket to the airport at the subway station.
why: 刚才 points to one finished purchase with a counted object, so 了 sits right after 买. 过 would say I have bought one at some time in my life, which does not fit 刚才.

q: 他每个周末都踢___足球。
zh: 他每个周末都踢足球。
py: tā měi ge zhōu mò dōu tī zú qiú
en: He plays football every weekend.
why: 每个周末…都 marks a habit, and a habit is not a single finished event, so no 了. 了 would turn it into one completed occasion, and 过 would mean 'has experienced'.

zh: 他没带地图出门。
py: tā méi dài dì tú chū mén
en: He didn't take a map when he went out.
why: 没 negates 带 and the verb stays bare, so the spare 了 is not used. The 没带地图 part can also follow 出门.

q: 我爸爸常常在公园里下___棋。
zh: 我爸爸常常在公园里下棋。
py: wǒ bà ba cháng cháng zài gōng yuán lǐ xià qí
en: My dad often plays chess in the park.
why: 常常 shows a regular habit, so there is no 了 after 下. 了 would present one completed game, and 的 and 地 are not verb endings.

s: 我们小时候每天都在河边玩，天黑了才回家。
zh: 我们小时候每天都在河边玩，天黑了才回家。
py: wǒ men xiǎo shí hou měi tiān dōu zài hé biān wán tiān hēi le cái huí jiā
en: When we were kids we played by the river every day and only went home when it got dark.
why: 每天都 makes 玩 a habit, so it takes no 了. The 了 in 天黑了 is a separate change of state (it has got dark), so both parts are correct.

s: 上个周末我在家，我的哥哥也在家。
zh: 上个周末我在家，我的哥哥也在家。
py: shàng ge zhōu mò wǒ zài jiā wǒ de gē ge yě zài jiā
en: Last weekend I was at home, and my brother was at home too.
why: 在 says where someone was, a state, so it takes no 了 even in the past; 上个周末 supplies the time. Adding 了 after 在 would be wrong.

s: 我昨天忘了带手机，所以没给你打电话。
zh: 我昨天忘了带手机，所以没给你打电话。
py: wǒ zuó tiān wàng le dài shǒu jī suǒ yǐ méi gěi nǐ dǎ diàn huà
en: I forgot to bring my phone yesterday, so I didn't call you.
why: 没 denies the call, so 打 stays bare with no 了. 忘了 is a separate finished event, so its 了 is right.
